Remove the codex seat from the panel of a critical change (#296)

Under the maintainer decision of Entry 257 (2026-11-27), recorded for
TODO 313, a critical change, a security-control review included, is
never sent to codex. Its panel is claude plus gemini only, its
convergence needs both seats, and the third family is recorded as
unavailable by that decision, which is how this project now meets the
vendored clause that a critical change adds a third family. A change
that is not critical keeps its codex seat from the sixth DISCOVERY
round onwards, on a neutral brief, as Entry 90 set.

.claude/rules/external/verifier-panel.md and the CODEX ROLE LIMIT and
VERIFIER DIVERSITY paragraphs of .claude/commands/flow.md now state
that rule. An owed codex seat is filled only from the sixth DISCOVERY
round of a change that is not critical. The codex stand-in for an
unreachable gemini, and the reassignment of the seat of any other
unreachable family to codex, apply only to a change that is not
critical; on a critical change such a seat stays owed. Entry 257
supersedes, for a critical change, the codex seat that Entry 124 gave
it and the coordinator rulings that put codex on its panel.

tools/check-flow-mode.py takes the 2 new pinned sha256 values of those
paragraphs that the check itself reports; no other line changes.

The vendored verifier-diversity rule and its corpus copy stay
byte-identical. The definition of a critical change, the floor that it
is never graded light, the rule that no second pass by a family already
on the panel fills a seat, and the tests and the lint are unchanged.
